fields.status_summary: Scope delivered: three-crate layering (compact-terminal-api + compact-terminal-cli + compact-terminal-mcp) following peek-api pattern. 4096-byte default inline limit with spill-and-peek behavior for oversized output. Latent bug fix: enable_tools() now called in get_info() so tools are visible to agents. Validation: cargo build warning-free, all tests pass (8+6+6), spec health 0 issues, MCP capability verification confirms tools advertised. Spec 63c60c9d promoted to approved.

Remaining work is a single docs edit plus a follow-up commit. Note: prior turn reported commit ef33ea60; review located submodule commit 68c4167 -- hash needs reconciling.

fields.status_summary: Complete. Three-crate layering (compact-terminal-api / -cli / -mcp) verified genuine: MCP and CLI both delegate to the shared API core. enable_tools() latent-bug fix present in get_info() with regression guard asserting tools.is_some() -- before the fix, run and read_spill were invisible to every agent in the repo. 4096-byte inline limit and spill behavior preserved and exercised end-to-end. 20 tests pass (8 api / 6 mcp / 6 cli). No new external dependencies: the superproject Cargo.lock delta adds only the two new workspace members, all deps pre-existing. Audited peek-mcp, ticket-mcp, feedback-mcp -- all call enable_tools() correctly, so the capability bug was isolated to compact-terminal-mcp. Commits: ef33ea60 (superproject; code + submodule pointer bump to memory-api 68c4167) and 16fe7334 (docs). Both hashes verified real in their respective repos. Docs criterion closed: tool-output.instructions.md now documents compact-terminal-cli as the MCP-unavailable fallback with run/read-spill examples and literal-substring grep semantics.
